$comment: Realisation (docs/rules-design.md, sections 2 and 4; ADR 0145, 0146): a lexeme in a cell made into its lexical form by blocking, stem templates, affix blocks, allomorphs and ordered rewrite rules, each step with its rule and branch. realise/blocking, realise/rewrite, realise/token, realise/paradigm and realise/error run on zz, an invented fixture language given whole; realise/apc runs apc's own rules and lexicon (lexicons/apc/language.yaml, lexemes.yaml), with `spellings: false` (forms that pin spellings only passed over, as the compiler's check of the tokens does), each a form the course writes but where a vector says otherwise.

vectors.note: No form of the lexeme fits: the rule's stem and its 1sg exponent; the boundary is kept.
A listed form covering the cell is the whole answer (fue): no rule runs, the listed part is named.
A listed stem is what the rule's blocks continue (tuv + e).
Of two pinned forms that fit, the more specific (Tense, Person, Number) wins over the stem (Tense).
Where the specific form does not fit, the stem continues.
Two forms as specific as each other fit the cell and neither is free: a tie.
Two free variants for the cell are no tie: the first is shown.
Blocking off ignores the listed stem: the regularised form (ADR 0145).
Blocking off ignores a listed whole form too.
A pinned stem is kept with blocking off: a pinned form never yields a regularised one.
A stated class selects its rule.
Blocking off ignores stated classes: the regular rule.
A cell that leaves Person out: no exponent that reads Person applies, and nothing completes the cell; the elsewhere exponent does.
The citation cell with no rule: the lexeme's own form.
A lexeme cited in a cell of its own (`citation` on the entry: apc's 2a3ed, cited as its participle), no rule: its own form.
A lexeme with a citation of its own is not cited in its category's cell: no rule holds there.
No rule holds and the cell is not the citation cell.
A lexeme the lexicon lacks.
A base with radicals and no stem template for it.
A lexical form the engine does not build (a listed item's parts).
Blocking finds a pinned form with spellings only: no lexical form to give.

`spellings: false` passes over a form that pins spellings only (no form, no stem), as the compiler's check of the course's tokens does (docs/rules-design.md, stage 2): the rules give sp+e, where blocking alone finds nothing to give (realise/error/spelled-only).

Two forms that pin spellings only for one cell are two spellings, not two lexical forms: no lexicon.tie (realise/error/lexicon-tie needs forms with `form` or `stem`); the lexicon compiles and the rules give sp+e.
A set of letters on both sides of the letter rewritten: f between vowels.
`before`, a list of which any will do: k before e.
k before a: no rule matches, nothing changes and no step is recorded.
`after`: d after a vowel.
d first in the form: nothing before it.
`at: end`: g last in the form.
g first: `at: end` does not hold.
`map` maps each letter its set matches.
A set of marks: a vowel with one of them, copied with its mark into `to`.
`after: #`: only at the form's edge, not the x at its end.
+? matches no boundary, and `to` writes none.
A boundary named in the pattern: n + p across the join of two lexemes.
+? matches the boundary, and `to` writes it again where `find` had it.
An allomorph by what it follows (`after: {endsIn: '{C}'}`).
The allomorph with no condition, elsewhere.
A paradigm: each cell realised or not.
Two forms for one set of values, not both free: the lexicon does not compile.
A pattern naming a set the notation lacks: the language does not compile.

The dative -li after a vowel (la-1sg's allomorph `after: {endsIn: .*+?[اىي]}`): دقّيلي, de22ili, as the course writes it.
No helping vowel where the ending begins with a vowel: -a, her, puts its fatha on the past's -t (a carrier), so no cluster is left: شفتها, shefta (s.phone.20).
A clitic before its word, by what it stands before (`before: {startsIn: '{V}'}`): d+adu.
The same clitic before a consonant: its allomorph with no condition, de+bag.
A word's own form chosen by the next word (`before: {pos: NOUN}`, `next`: its base lexeme): mile before a noun, as apc's teens say their r (7da3shar sene).
The same word with no next word: its own form.

A base whose own form has an allomorph by what follows (`before: {startsIn: '{C}'}`), before an ending that begins with a vowel: its own form, kann+es (the ending chosen by the base, then the base by the ending: two passes).
The same base before another vowel: kann+in.
Before an ending that begins with a consonant the base takes its allomorph: kan+n (as apc's bad- before -na).
A rewrite with `when` holds of a token whose base it holds of (a noun): kase.
The same rewrite does not hold of a verb.
A lexeme whose form is a string, in its own citation cell, is that form: no rule runs (zz-present would hold).
`pinned: false`: every pinned form passed over (what the rules alone give): v+e, not the pinned vi.
A phrase's form written over several tokens: the word a token writes (`word`, from 0), its other lexemes joined to it: dia+s.
A phrase whole cannot take an affix: name the word it goes on.

As the bundle's paradigms are listed (strict): a cell no exponent of the rule names (the present's you) gives nothing, where the rule's other cells give their forms.
Not strict, the same cell is the bare stem: the rule holds, and no exponent applies.
apc's noun rule has only a feminine: strict, a noun's plural is no-rule, never the singular (broken plurals are lexemes of their own).
Strict, a phrase lexeme has no paradigm: its words are no word's cells.
A rule with no blocks (an adjective that does not agree) still gives its stem when strict.

stanna's command stem (an alef written and not said, then a cluster) after the 1sg's alef, its listed stem passed over: the alef not said goes, and the cluster gives the prefix its vowel (estanna). Before this rule the prefix's alef took a sukun, and Arabizi kept it as an Arabic letter.
stanna, a stem written whole that ends in its vowel, before the past's -t: -ay- as the templates' defective-ay stem gives (stannayt; the course's eshtarayti). It was ...ىت, stannat.
a7la's class (invariable) passed over, as a regularised form is: the feminine ending takes the place of the stem's last vowel, as a defective verb's does (a7le). Before this rule it was أحلىة, a7lىe.
a7la is invariable (a comparative does not agree, Kline p. 14): its feminine is itself.
The 1sg's alef goes before a glide with a vowel as before any consonant with one (wa22ef, as Form II's 3allem). It took a sukun before, and Arabizi kept it as an Arabic letter (اwa22ef).
